# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by docs/generate_configuration.py from the code: do not edit by hand. Regenerate it after changing config/schema.py, cli.py, config/load.py, a preset or a stage config; docs/check_docs.py fails while it is out of date. -->

A run is configured by one TOML file, optionally based on a built-in preset, with command-line options and `--set SECTION.KEY=VALUE` overrides on top. Later sources win, key by key: schema defaults < preset < TOML file < command-line options < `--set`. The resolved configuration is written to `OUTPUT/config.toml` and into every run record; it loads again unchanged. Only the scientific sections (all but `[run]`, `[execution]` and `[reports]`) can change results; [usage](usage.md) explains the commands and the run directory.

`--set` takes TOML values: `--set quality.read_calibration=false`, `--set execution.cores=32`, `--set 'input.contigs=["chr1", "chr2"]'`; a value that is not valid TOML is read as a string.

Contents:

- [Command-line options](#command-line-options)
- [TOML settings](#toml-settings)
- [Consistency rules](#consistency-rules)
- [Presets](#presets)
- [Internal model constants](#internal-model-constants)
- [Environment](#environment)

## Command-line options

`haplotypes COMMAND --help` prints the same options. `python -m haplotype_reconstruction` is the same program. Options of `run` override the configuration file; their default is the configuration's value.

### haplotypes run

Run or resume the pipeline.

```text
usage: haplotypes run [-h] [--preset {tromau,aulstu}] [--vcf VCF] [--templates TEMPLATES] [--output OUTPUT]
                      [--checkpoints CHECKPOINTS] [--cores CORES] [--memory-limit MEMORY_LIMIT]
                      [--contigs CONTIGS [CONTIGS ...]] [--stop-after {discovery,painting}] [--serial]
                      [--max-contigs MAX_CONTIGS] [--process-contigs PROCESS_CONTIGS [PROCESS_CONTIGS ...]]
                      [--batch-queue BATCH_QUEUE] [--set SECTION.KEY=VALUE]
                      [config]
```

| option | value | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config` (optional) |  |  | TOML configuration (paths relative to the working directory). |
| `--preset` | `{tromau,aulstu}` |  | Built-in base configuration. |
| `--vcf` | `VCF` |  | Input VCF/BCF with FORMAT/AD ([input] vcf). |
| `--templates` | `TEMPLATES` |  | Simulate from these founder templates ([simulation] templates; sets [input] kind = "simulation"). |
| `--output` | `OUTPUT` |  | Run directory ([run] output). |
| `--checkpoints` | `CHECKPOINTS` |  | Checkpoint directory ([run] checkpoints). |
| `--cores` | `CORES` |  | CPU ceiling ([execution] cores; default: affinity). |
| `--memory-limit` | `MEMORY_LIMIT` |  | Memory the run may plan to use at once, e.g. 200G ([execution] memory_limit; default: available at start minus headroom). |
| `--contigs` | `CONTIGS ...` |  | Contigs in order ([input] contigs). |
| `--stop-after` | `{discovery,painting}` |  | [run] stop_after. |
| `--serial` |  |  | [execution] serial. |
| `--max-contigs` | `MAX_CONTIGS` |  | [execution] max_contigs (implies --serial). |
| `--process-contigs` | `PROCESS_CONTIGS ...` |  | Shard: [execution] process_contigs. |
| `--batch-queue` | `BATCH_QUEUE` |  | [execution] batch_queue. |
| `--set` | `SECTION.KEY=VALUE` |  | Override one setting (repeatable), e.g. quality.read_calibration=false. |

### haplotypes status

Run records and checkpoint progress (no payload decoding).

```text
usage: haplotypes status [-h] [--checkpoints CHECKPOINTS] [--contigs CONTIGS [CONTIGS ...]] [--json] RUN
```

| option | value | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RUN` |  |  |  |
| `--checkpoints` | `CHECKPOINTS` |  |  |
| `--contigs` | `CONTIGS ...` |  |  |
| `--json` |  |  | Print the report as JSON. |

### haplotypes recombination

Run or resume the recombination stage of a run whose family phase is recorded and republish its tables (a recorded stage keeps its settings: changed settings need a new output root).

```text
usage: haplotypes recombination [-h] [--order-breakpoints ORDER_BREAKPOINTS] [--cores CORES]
                                [--set recombination.KEY=VALUE]
                                RUN
```

| option | value | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RUN` |  |  |  |
| `--order-breakpoints` | `ORDER_BREAKPOINTS` |  | [recombination] order_breakpoints TSV. |
| `--cores` | `CORES` |  |  |
| `--set` | `recombination.KEY=VALUE` |  |  |

### haplotypes evaluate


| `RUN` |  |  |  |

### haplotypes export

Write a finished run's founder VCF and phased sample VCF (the files of the run's export stage, OUTPUT/export) to a new directory, optionally with per-component founder-track TSVs.

```text
usage: haplotypes export [-h] [--products {founders,samples,tracks} [{founders,samples,tracks} ...]]
                         [--format {vcf,bcf}] [--full-length | --no-full-length] [--vcf VCF]
                         [--contigs CONTIGS [CONTIGS ...]] [--cores CORES]
                         RUN DEST
```

| option | value | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RUN` |  |  |  |
| `DEST` |  |  | New or empty directory. |
| `--products` | `{founders,samples,tracks} ...` | founders samples | founders: per-contig founder VCF (haploid GT, one column c<component>_H<row> per founder row); samples: phased sample VCF (GT:PS); tracks: per-component founder-track TSV.gz (CHROM POS H0 H1 ...). |
| `--format` | `{vcf,bcf}` | vcf | vcf: bgzipped VCF with a tabix index (CSI beyond 2^29 bp); bcf: BCF with a CSI index. |
| `--full-length`, `--no-full-length` |  |  | Write every input biallelic SNP that reached the site filter (FILTER PASS for kept sites, the rule codes r1-r5 for removed ones); --no-full-length writes the kept sites only. |
| `--vcf` | `VCF` |  | Original input VCF/BCF (normally recovered from the run; simulations need none: their abstract alleles are written as A/C). |
| `--contigs` | `CONTIGS ...` |  |  |
| `--cores` | `CORES` |  |  |

## TOML settings

A configuration file holds the sections below; every key is optional. A key or section that is not listed here is an error naming the valid keys. Values are type-checked; paths are resolved against the working directory when the file is loaded; an empty path string means unset.

### Top level

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | string: `"tromau"`, `"aulstu"` | `""` | Built-in base configuration: tromau or aulstu. |

### [run]

Where results go and where to stop.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `output` | path | `""` (unset) | Run directory (outputs, logs, run records); default work/runs/<preset or input kind>[_seed<seed>]. |
| `checkpoints` | path | `""` (unset) | Checkpoint directory; default OUTPUT/checkpoints. |
| `stop_after` | string: `"discovery"`, `"painting"` | `""` | Stop cleanly after this stage: discovery, or painting (per-contig work done, genome-wide stages not started); empty runs everything. |

### [execution]

CPUs, lanes and shards (never part of results).

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cores` | "auto" or integer >= 1 | `"auto"` | Total CPU ceiling (processes x threads); auto = CPU affinity. |
| `contig_lanes` | "auto" or integer >= 1 | `"auto"` | Contigs reconstructed concurrently; auto = one lane per 16 cores, limited by memory; 1 = one contig at a time with all cores. |
| `memory_limit` | "auto", integer bytes, or a size with a binary unit (K, M, G, T), e.g. "200G" | `"auto"` | Memory the run may plan to use at once (the memory governor paces work to fit; results never depend on it): a size such as "200G" (binary units), or auto = memory available at start minus a 10% headroom. |
| `serial` | boolean | `false` | Discover, assemble and paint one contig at a time, each recorded before the next (short allocations). |
| `max_contigs` | integer >= 0 | `0` | Finish at most this many more contigs in this invocation, then stop cleanly (0 = no limit; > 0 implies serial). |
| `process_contigs` | array of strings | `[]` | Shard: process only these contigs (of [input] contigs) through painting; no genome-wide stages. |
| `batch_queue` | path | `""` (unset) | Shared directory through which batch-worker helper allocations take local-selection fits and hierarchy join batches. |
| `profile` | boolean | `false` | Print per-phase timings and thread-allocation traces. |

### [input]

Observations and contigs.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string: `"vcf"`, `"simulation"` | `"vcf"` | Observations: an indexed VCF/BCF with FORMAT/AD, or a simulation from founder templates. |
| `vcf` | path | `""` (unset) | Input VCF/BCF (kind = vcf). |
| `contigs` | array of strings | `[]` | Contigs to analyse, in order (required unless the preset lists them). |

### [samples]

Optional sample metadata.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata` | path | `""` (unset) | Metadata workbook (.xlsx) describing the samples. |
| `sheet` | string | `"main_data"` | Workbook sheet. |
| `id_column` | string | `"primary_ID"` | Column holding the VCF sample IDs. |
| `generation_column` | string | `"generation"` | Column holding generation/cohort labels. |
| `sex_column` | string | `"sex"` | Column holding recorded sex (F/M). |
| `reference_generation` | string | `""` | Generation whose rows the reference-consistency report compares with discovered blocks (e.g. G0). |
| `generation_prefixes` | array of strings | `[]` | Labels starting with one of these are read as that prefix (e.g. G0 for G0_AulStu). |
| `generations` | array of strings | `[]` | Allowed generation labels (empty: any). |
| `sexes` | array of strings | `[]` | Allowed sex labels (empty: any). |

### [quality]

Evidence quality control and read model.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `site_filter` | string: `"auto"`, `"on"`, `"off"` | `"auto"` | Self-calibrated per-contig site filter; auto = on for VCF input, off for simulations. |
| `sample_filter` | string: `"auto"`, `"on"`, `"off"` | `"auto"` | Per-contig library-contamination QC (flagged samples leave founder construction); auto = on for VCF input, off for simulations; it runs only where the site filter is applied. |
| `read_calibration` | boolean | `true` | Fit read error, allelic balance and overdispersion from the observed AD; off = fixed binomial model (error 0.02). |

### [genetic_map]

Inference genetic map.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rate_cm_per_mb` | number | `5.0` | Fallback recombination rate (cM/Mb) without a map or beyond its knots. |
| `file` | path | `""` (unset) | Cumulative cM map (PLINK, or chromosome/position_bp/map_cm TSV). |

### [pedigree]

Pedigree inference.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `evidence_calibration` | string: `"predictive"`, `"off"` | `"predictive"` | Cross-chromosome pedigree evidence scaling: predictive, or off for unscaled evidence. |

### [pedigree.eligibility]

Who may be whose parent.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy` | string: `"none"`, `"constraints"`, `"cohorts"` | `"none"` | Parent candidates: none (every sample), constraints (JSON file), cohorts (workbook generations). |
| `constraints` | path | `""` (unset) | JSON constraints (policy = constraints): candidate_parents, excluded_samples, ineligible_children, direction_supported_edges. |
| `parent_generations` | table of strings | `{}` | Cohorts: child generation -> parent generation, e.g. {F2 = "F1", F3 = "F2"}. |
| `opposite_sex_pairs` | boolean | `true` | Cohorts: two-parent configurations need one recorded female and one recorded male. |

### [family_phase]

Family phase.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `protected_intervals` | path | `""` (unset) | TSV of intervals (chrom, start, end, reason) where family phase keeps its frames. |

### [recombination]

Recombination maps.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shared_family_evidence` | boolean | `true` | Use shared-family phase-error evidence in the maps. |
| `order_breakpoints` | path | `""` (unset) | TSV of reference-order breakpoints (chrom, start, end, reason). |

### [export]

Final products: founder and sample VCFs.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Write the final products at the end of a complete run (OUTPUT/export): per contig a founder VCF (haploid GT, one column c<component>_H<row> per founder row) and the phased sample VCF (GT:PS), bgzipped with tabix indexes. |
| `full_length` | boolean | `true` | Write every input biallelic SNP that reached the site filter (FILTER PASS for kept sites, the rule codes r1-r5 for removed ones); false writes only the kept sites. |

### [reports]

Optional reports.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reference_consistency` | boolean | `false` | Compare discovered blocks with the reference-generation rows ([samples] reference_generation). |

### [simulation]

Simulation (input kind = simulation).

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | integer >= 0 or "random" | `400` | Simulation seed, or "random" (the realised seed is recorded). |
| `templates` | path | `""` (unset) | Directory of chromosome NPZ founder templates. |
| `cohorts` | array of integers | `[20, 100, 200]` | Individuals in successive cohorts. |
| `depth` | number | `5.0` | Mean read depth. |
| `generating_rate_cm_per_mb` | number | `5.0` | Generating fallback recombination rate. |
| `generating_map` | path | `""` (unset) | Generating genetic map (independent of inference). |
| `backcross_fraction` | number | `0.0` | Fraction of later matings with an actual parent. |
| `backcross_start_cohort` | integer >= 0 | `3` | First cohort with backcrosses. |
| `observe_cohorts` | array of integers | `[]` | Only sequence these cohorts (empty: all). |
| `observed_fraction` | number | `1.0` | Random fraction of eligible individuals sequenced. |

### [simulation.reads]

Generating read model.

| key | type | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `error_rate` | number | `0.02` | Generating sequencing error rate. |
| `depth_cv` | number | `0.0` | Between-sample depth coefficient of variation. |
| `heterozygote_alt_probability` | number | `0.5` | Alternate-read probability in heterozygotes. |
| `dropout_fraction` | number | `0.0` | Contiguous missing-marker fraction per sample. |
| `read_length_bp` | integer >= 0 | `0` | Read length; > 0 samples paired-end fragments shared by neighbouring sites. |
| `fragment_mean_bp` | number | `375.0` | Mean fragment length (read_length_bp > 0). |
| `fragment_sd_bp` | number | `150.0` | Fragment length standard deviation. |

## Consistency rules

Checked when the configuration is loaded, before any input is read (the error messages of `config/load.py`). Checks that need the inputs (VCF header, workbook, contig counts) run next, still before any computation; see [usage](usage.md#checks-before-computation).

- [execution] max_contigs runs contigs serially; it cannot be combined with serial = false
- serial contigs are painted before the next is discovered; they cannot stop after discovery
- [input] contigs is required (no preset lists them)
- [input] contigs must be unique
- [execution] process_contigs must be unique
- [execution] process_contigs must be a subset of [input] contigs
- [execution] process_contigs (a shard) and serial cannot be combined
- [input] kind = "vcf" needs [input] vcf (or --vcf)
- [simulation] settings need [input] kind = "simulation": ...
- [input] kind = "simulation" needs [simulation] templates (or --templates)
- [input] vcf is not read by simulations (templates are built with the templates command)
- simulations take neither [samples] metadata nor a parent-eligibility policy
- [pedigree.eligibility] policy = "cohorts" needs [samples] metadata
- [pedigree.eligibility] policy = "cohorts" needs parent_generations
- [pedigree.eligibility] parent_generations needs policy = "cohorts"
- [pedigree.eligibility] policy = "constraints" and a constraints file go together
- [reports] reference_consistency needs [samples] reference_generation
- [samples] reference_generation needs [samples] metadata
- [simulation] cohorts must be positive sizes

## Presets

`preset = "NAME"` (or `--preset NAME`) starts from a built-in configuration; the file, command-line options and `--set` override it key by key. Presets hold no data paths.

### tromau

```toml
# TroMau cross (AcTm BCF): the 22 autosomes; workbook cohorts F2 <- F1 with opposite-sex parent pairs. All samples are
# analysed, including the four G0 rows (as in base); the G0 rows are the reference generation of the consistency
# report. The data paths ([input] vcf, [samples] metadata) come from the user's configuration.
[input]
kind = "vcf"
contigs = ["chr1", "chr2", "chr3", "chr4", "chr5", "chr6", "chr7", "chr8", "chr9", "chr10", "chr11", "chr12",
           "chr13", "chr14", "chr15", "chr16", "chr17", "chr18", "chr19", "chr20", "chr22", "chr23"]

[samples]
sheet = "main_data"
id_column = "primary_ID"
generation_column = "generation"
sex_column = "sex"
reference_generation = "G0"

[pedigree.eligibility]
policy = "cohorts"
parent_generations = { F2 = "F1" }
opposite_sex_pairs = true

[reports]
reference_consistency = true
```

### aulstu

```toml
# AulStu cross (AsAc BCF): the 22 autosomes; workbook cohorts F2 <- F1 and F3 <- F2 with opposite-sex parent pairs.
# Generation labels starting with G0 (species-labelled founders) read as G0; labels must be G0, F1, F2 or F3 and
# sexes F or M. The data paths ([input] vcf, [samples] metadata) come from the user's configuration.
[input]
kind = "vcf"
contigs = ["chr1", "chr2", "chr3", "chr4", "chr5", "chr6", "chr7", "chr8", "chr9", "chr10", "chr11", "chr12",
           "chr13", "chr14", "chr15", "chr16", "chr17", "chr18", "chr19", "chr20", "chr22", "chr23"]

[samples]
sheet = "main_data"
id_column = "primary_ID"
generation_column = "generation"
sex_column = "sex"
generation_prefixes = ["G0"]
generations = ["G0", "F1", "F2", "F3"]
sexes = ["F", "M"]

[pedigree.eligibility]
policy = "cohorts"
parent_generations = { F2 = "F1", F3 = "F2" }
opposite_sex_pairs = true
```

## Internal model constants

Each stage has a frozen configuration whose defaults are the production values. They are model constants, not settings: no TOML key or option changes them, except the fields marked *set by* a TOML key. They enter the stage's checkpoint identity, so results always record them. The [methods](methods/README.md) explain them; a methods page cites a constant as `RootConfig.path = value`, which `docs/check_docs.py` checks against these defaults.

### EvidenceConfig

Stage `evidence`, `evidence/config.py`. Evidence stage: loader policy -> site/sample QC -> read model -> likelihoods -> blocks.

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block_sites` | `200` | Discovery block width in sites (consecutive, non-overlapping windows of the site axis). |
| **discovery_sites** (DiscoverySiteRule) |  | Minimum read support for discovery, independent of cohort size. |
| `discovery_sites.minimum_total_depth` | `5` |  |
| **site_quality** (SiteQualityConfig) |  | Self-calibrated site filter r1-r5 (``evidence/site_quality.py``). |
| `site_quality.enabled` | `True` | *Set by* `[quality] site_filter`. |
| `site_quality.classification_error` | `0.01` | Read model used only to classify each sample's genotype at a site; the clean-core error rate and allele balance are then fitted, not these. |
| `site_quality.classification_heterozygote_alt` | `0.5` |  |
| `site_quality.core_posterior_level` | `0.5` | r1/r2 windows: where the fitted core's local posterior is >= this level (histogram smoothed over this many bins). |
| `site_quality.histogram_smoothing_bins` | `5` |  |
| `site_quality.clean_posterior_level` | `0.5` | r3/r4: a site is flagged when P(clean core) < this level, and only if the artefact class is separated from the clean core by this factor (rate ratio, or binomial standard deviations at the median depth). |
| `site_quality.minimum_artefact_separation` | `3.0` |  |
| `site_quality.drop_uninformative_sites` | `True` | r5 (informativeness, not quality): fewer expected carriers of a non-major genotype than this. It removes sites without segregating information. |
| `site_quality.minimum_expected_carriers` | `2.0` |  |
| `site_quality.minimum_calibration_sites` | `1000` | Contigs with fewer biallelic SNPs than this are not filtered. |
| **sample_quality** (SampleQualityConfig) |  | Per-sample, per-contig contamination QC (``evidence/sample_quality.py``). |
| `sample_quality.enabled` | `True` | *Set by* `[quality] sample_filter`. |
| `sample_quality.flag_robust_z` | `5.0` | Extreme-outlier bar on the variance-stabilised scale (real TroMau, 22 contigs: samples without a contamination signature reach at most z 4.0). |
| `sample_quality.minimum_samples` | `20` | The median/MAD spread needs a cohort; smaller cohorts flag nothing. |
| `sample_quality.fragment_bp` | `1000` | Cells of one sample closer than one sequenced fragment can share reads: one event. |
| `sample_quality.segment_gap_bp` | `1000000` | Inherited-segment report only: heterozygous near-private events of one (sample, partner) less than segment_gap_bp apart form a region; regions with fewer events are not listed. |
| `sample_quality.segment_minimum_events` | `3.0` |  |
| **read_model** (ReadModelConfig) |  | Held-out calibration of the observed-AD read model (``evidence/read_model``). |
| `read_model.enabled` | `True` | *Set by* `[quality] read_calibration`. |
| `read_model.marker_stride` | `8` |  |
| `read_model.maximum_fit_depth` | `48` |  |
| `read_model.fold_window_bp` | `1000000` |  |
| `read_model.em_starts` | `((0.02, 0.5), (0.01, 0.35), (0.08, 0.65))` |  |
| `read_model.em_maximum_iterations` | `2000` |  |
| `read_model.em_tolerance_per_observation` | `1e-10` |  |
| `read_model.initial_heterozygote_concentration` | `40.0` | Start of the joint fit's shared heterozygote concentration (kappa). |
| `read_model.lookup_depth` | `64` | Likelihood application: cells up to this depth come from a per-sample lookup table, deeper cells are evaluated directly (a performance setting, not a depth filter). |
| `fixed_error` | `0.02` | Fallback read model: binomial with this symmetric error and heterozygote ALT fraction 1/2. |

### DiscoveryConfig

Stage `discovery`, `discovery/config.py`. All raw-discovery settings (one record identity).

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **model** (FixedKModelConfig) |  | The hard fixed-K factorisation H (K binary rows) x A (each sample's unordered row pair). |
| `model.unknown_copy_penalty` | `0.5` | nats charged per unknown copy at every observed site (lambda). |
| `model.snps_per_bin` | `10` | sites per bin of the switching Viterbi cost (one bin per site when a block has at most this many discovery sites). |
| `model.switch_penalty` | `10.0` | nats per switch of a sample's diploid state between adjacent bins. |
| `model.max_iterations` | `50` | coordinate-descent iterations (A step + H step) per fit. |
| **cavity** (CavityScoreConfig) |  | Fixed-assignment leave-one-sample-out mean-field cavity score of one panel. |

### LocalSelectionConfig

Stage `local_selection`, `local_selection/config.py`. All local-selection settings (one record identity per round).

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **model** (PathModelConfig) |  | The copying model of a block. |
| `model.unknown_mass` | `0.01` | fixed prior mass of the unknown state (base ``background_mass``; also the background-state mass of the context refit's bin-level HMM). |

The redraw probability is r = 1 - exp(-redraw_rate_per_morgan x Morgans), using the contig's genetic map. A redraw can choose the same state; this is not the observed founder-switch rate or a sample's generation label. Independent of assembly's gap horizon. |
| **search** (PathSearchConfig) |  | Drop / merge / add search with GEM refits (search.py, fit.py). |

| `search.refits_per_kind_cap` | `16` | release 2.2: the proposal cut takes whole tie classes of the screened score (at decision_tolerance) until at least refits_per_kind; a class that would take the refits of a kind past this cap is left out whole (counted as an overflow; no member of a tie class is preferred to another). |
| `search.round_backstop_base` | `10` |  |
| `search.round_backstop_per_founder` | `2` |  |
| `search.update_backstop_base` | `20` |  |
| `search.update_backstop_per_founder` | `4` |  |
| `search.update_backstop_per_site` | `2` |  |
| `search.tolerance` | `1e-06` | the GEM fit's own tolerance (frequency-step acceptance, flip gains, convergence; nats). |
| `search.decision_tolerance` | `0.0009765625` | tie quantum of every decision between EM-fitted or screened objectives (release 2.1): the proposal cut per kind, the round winner and the stop of the climb, the start-or-incumbent choice and the keep-incumbent rule between rounds; values chained within it are tied and decided by content (fewer founders, then the canonical panel bytes). A power of two placed by the valley census far above EM convergence residuals and the motion of 1e-9 relative GL noise, far below genuine drop / merge / add differences (nats). |
| **bank** (CandidateBankConfig) |  | Candidate-bank search (bank.py): refits of the context proposals with discovery's fixed-K model, ranked by its binned-Viterbi BIC, K * complexity_scale * (L / 200) * N_active - 2 log L; K-scaled reported backstops with K the current panel's founder count: at most start_backstop(K) novel starts per call, score_backstop(K) admitted panels, round_backstop(K) rounds. Release 2.1: the block's discovery tie quanta (maths.ties BlockQuanta of the fixed-K workspace) order the BIC selection and the cavity-best endpoints (kind ``nll``) and stop the rounds (an improvement must exceed the ``improvement`` quantum). |

| `bank.start_backstop_base` | `512` |  |
| `bank.start_backstop_per_founder` | `64` |  |
| `bank.complexity_scale` | `0.5` |  |
| **release** (PathReleaseConfig) |  | Release of a selected panel's alleles (release.py): the one-bit conditional allele probability reaches ``min_call_probability`` and the favourable samples (whose own evidence favours the allele by more than ``favourable_margin`` nats) include ``min_supporters`` carriers by count (posterior carrier probability above 1/2) or by expected carrier mass. Release 2.1: ``favourable_margin`` is the ``cell`` tie quantum of maths.ties (2^-23 nats; the 1e-9 of 2.0 sat at the motion of 1e-9 GL noise, so a symmetric-evidence cell, whose gain is exactly 0, straddled it). ``unknown_count_band``: a site's MAP number of unknown copies (0, 1, 2; it feeds assembly completion's all-or-nothing veto) must win by more than this relative posterior margin, else the smaller count (the ``probability`` tie quantum of maths.ties, 2^-20; design A-7: an integer count whose posterior masses can tie exactly). |

### AssemblyConfig

Stage `assembly`, `assembly/config.py`. Assembly of local panels into chromosome-scale founder components.

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `batch_size` | `10` | input components per joined batch at every level (base L1 and L2-L4 both 10). |
| `minimum_levels` | `4` | hierarchy levels that run (while they reduce the component count) before the loop may stop because only phase breaks separate the remaining components; base ran exactly four levels, so at today's sizes (<= 10^4 blocks per break-free segment) the level schedule is base's. Beyond it a level runs only while a boundary that is not a phase break remains (base stopped at level 4 regardless: B4). |
| `min_boundary_informative_samples` | `4` | a boundary between adjacent components becomes a phase break (never joined) when fewer samples are informative on both sides. |
| `gap_horizon_scale` | `3` | inverse-Morgan scale of the linker and beam's maximum transition gap at levels >= 2: max(1, 1 + floor(recombination_tolerance / (mean component span in Morgans x gap_horizon_scale))). Level 1 uses every gap. This search-horizon control is independent of local selection's copying intensity. |
| `recombination_tolerance` | `0.5` | dimensionless span budget in the maximum-gap rule; divided by the mean component span in Morgans times gap_horizon_scale. |

A fixed constant, the same on every machine, so results never depend on free memory: 128 GiB is above base's own memory-derived cap on every reference node (at most a quarter of the available memory, about 120 GB), where base never fell back (largest frontier 76,776 paths, sim_s10001 chr3 L1); K = 30 synthetic and AulStu peaks (257 and 357 paths) are four orders of magnitude below it. The memory of large programmes is admitted by the run's memory governor (proposals.PROGRAMME_BUDGETS). |
| `refinement.alternative_branches` | `16` | complete same-level count continuations, including the ordinary path and all incoming panels. ### PaintingConfig

Stage `painting`, `painting/config.py`. Model constants of the painting HMM; defaults are the production values.

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `switch_penalty_per_snp` | `1.0` | nats per selected site of a bin subtracted from log(theta) for every track change; a change between bins of ``snps_per_bin`` sites costs about ``switch_penalty_per_snp * snps_per_bin`` nats more than its map probability (about 109 nats per track change in total at the defaults). |
| `robustness_epsilon` | `0.01` | uniform genotype-error mixture of the emission, P = (1 - eps) P(GL \| pair) + eps / 3 per observed site. |
| `double_recomb_factor` | `1.5` | exponent on the switch weight when both tracks change at one bin edge. |
| `snps_per_bin` | `100` | target selected sites per bin (bins split the selected sites into max(1, L // snps_per_bin) near-equal consecutive runs). |
| `emission_log_floor` | `-50.0` | lower bound of each site's log emission (nats). |
| `minimum_release_posterior` | `0.9` | tau of the release rule; a track pair is released when the posterior mass of its unordered class pair (or of its local allele-equivalence pair, if directly read-supported) is >= tau. Predeclared 10% within-model posterior-error budget. |
| `label_continuity_minimum_switch_gain` | `2.0` | a row-suffix relabelling must lower the painted switch total by at least this many switches. |
| `label_continuity_maximum_loser_ratio` | `0.1` | samples whose painted switches rise may be at most this fraction of the samples whose switches fall. |

| `direction.pair_failure_probability` | `0.02` | Pair-level painting-failure mixture bounding the orientation correction to [log(epsilon), log(2 - epsilon)]. Base shared this value with the M0 contamination (parent_state_contamination_probability); the two roles are now separate settings. |
| `direction.message_passes` | `4` | Synchronous cavity-message passes preparing the frozen short-ancestry path factor. |
| `direction.final_max_iterations` | `8192` | Final reciprocal solve: undamped, then a damped retry; residual measured before damping. |
| `direction.final_tolerance` | `1e-08` |  |
| `direction.retry_iterations` | `4096` |  |
| `direction.retry_damping` | `0.5` |  |
| `direction.ancestry_path_budget` | `16` | Top joint configurations per sample in the reverse two-edge path factor. |
| **selection** (SelectionConfig) |  | Marginal parent-state priors, M0 contamination and acyclic graph search. |
| `selection.state_priors` | `(0.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333)` |  |
| `selection.prior_sensitivity` | `((0.5, 0.3, 0.2), (0.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333), (0.2, 0.3, 0.5))` | Alternative fixed priors; an M0 call must survive all of them to be released. |
| `selection.m0_contamination_probability` | `0.02` | Each aggregated M1/M2 likelihood is mixed with the child's M0 likelihood at this weight. |
| `selection.graph_local_search_passes` | `3` |  |
| **resampling** (ResamplingConfig) |  | Chromosome bootstrap (seeded) and leave-one-chromosome-out refits. |
| `resampling.bootstrap_replicates` | `1000` |  |
| `resampling.bootstrap_seed` | `20260725` |  |
| **release** (ReleaseConfig) |  | Tier A / Tier B release rules (Tier B is the primary product). |
| `release.minimum_informative_contigs` | `3` |  |
| **release.tier_a** (TierThresholds) |  | Release cut-offs of one evidence tier (fractions of resampled fits). |
| `release.tier_a.configuration_bootstrap` | `0.95` |  |
| `release.tier_a.parent_bootstrap` | `0.95` |  |
| `release.tier_a.loco_fraction` | `0.95` |  |
| **release.tier_b** (TierThresholds) |  | Release cut-offs of one evidence tier (fractions of resampled fits). |
| `release.tier_b.configuration_bootstrap` | `0.7` |  |
| `release.tier_b.parent_bootstrap` | `0.7` |  |
| `release.tier_b.loco_fraction` | `0.8` |  |
| `release.orientation_reversal_probability` | `0.02` | A released inferred edge needs full-data orientation log odds >= log((1 - p) / p) (3.9 nats); caller chronology is exempt. |
| `release.support_set_coverage` | `0.95` | Candidate sets carry this much configuration probability mass. |
| **exclusion** (ExclusionConfig) |  | Full-marker Mendelian exclusion releasing M0/M1 counts without new edges. |
| `exclusion.alpha` | `0.01` |  |
| `exclusion.genotype_replacement_probability` | `0.01` |  |
| `exclusion.bet_sizes` | `(0.0009765625, 0.00390625, 0.015625, 0.0625, 0.25, 1.0)` |  |
| `exclusion.window_widths_bp` | `(1000000, 5000000, 20000000)` | Half-overlapping physical windows (bp), plus the whole chromosome. |

### FounderRefitConfig

Stage `founder_refit`, `founder_refit/config.py`. Defaults are the production values.

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `minimum_gain_nats` | `5.0` | prior per allele: a called allele changes only if the painted carriers' robust log likelihood improves by at least this much (5 nats: the assembled allele keeps prior odds of about 150 to 1); a swap of two rows' alleles changes two cells and needs twice this. |
| `coordinate_sweeps` | `3` | sweeps of single-row flips and two-row swaps per site. |

### FamilyPhaseConfig

Stage `family_phase`, `family_phase/config.py`. Pedigree-conditioned phase of one chromosome.

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transmission_error` | `0.001` | probability that a copy factor transmits the other parental allele. |
| `scaffold_phase_error` | `0.01` | probability that a root's scaffold orientation is wrong at a heterozygous site. |
| `phase_switch_probability` | `0.005` | probability of a frame switch at a painting-bin edge inside a component (the family phase chain and the polish's coarse bins); component edges switch with probability 1/2 and the family chain never switches phase inside a painting bin (the polish's refinement: polish_window_sites). |
| `map_max_sweeps` | `60` | safety cap on the sweeps of one ascent (release 2.2: both sweep tiers count; the two-schedule estimator runs up to three ascents). Every accepted step raises the posterior by more than a tie quantum, so the solver terminates by construction; reaching the cap is an error. Measured (19 Oct 2026): at most 9 sweeps (stress_n80), TroMau and std_n80 at most 4. |
| `map_long_moves` | `False` | run the long compound moves (change pairs longer than map_solver.LONG_SPAN sites and the |
| `root_frame_window_bp` | `500000.0` | flank reach W around a bin edge |
| `root_frame_location_bp` | `250000.0` | location tolerance (net votes ignore +- this around the edge) |
| `root_frame_minimum_children` | `3` | children needed to move a frame (also the junction guard's parent size) |
| `root_frame_informative_nats` | `2.0` | per-child vote threshold tau |
| `root_frame_max_rounds` | `8` | repair rounds |
| `protected_intervals` | `()` | *Set by* `[family_phase] protected_intervals`. (contig, start, end) closed bp intervals where no frame repair is made (reference-order breakpoints). |
| `polish_copy_error` | `0.01` | copy-consistency error of called scaffold alleles |
| `polish_window_sites` | `100` | fine phase boundaries allowed within this many sites of a current phase or selector change, inside the bin to the right of a bin edge (that edge's flip probability is split over them; the first painting bin of a chromosome or component has no such edge and stays rigid) |
| `polish_max_sweeps` | `6` | colour sweeps before the polish must have converged |
| `polish_minimum_gain` | `1e-06` | the polish's tie quantum q (nats): an interval is accepted only when its exact gain exceeds q, inside q the current configuration is kept (the score reads called scaffold alleles only, so q only has to exceed rounding) |
| `polish_minimum_biological_gain` | `0.0` | smallest copy-consistency gain for an interval that changes an observable phase, compared with a band of q. |

### RecombinationConfig

Stage `recombination`, `recombination/config.py`. Per-meiosis decoding and map aggregation.

| constant | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy_error` | `0.01` | probability that a transmitted allele reads as the other parental homologue |
| `artifact_rate` | `1e-08` | correlated orientation-artifact process of a meiosis (entry rate per bp, mean length) |
| `artifact_mean_bp` | `50000.0` | correlated orientation-artifact process of a meiosis (entry rate per bp, mean length) |
| `minimum_origin_probability` | `0.98` | posterior support of a marker's parental homologue (and of no artifact) for a called crossover |
| `maximum_gap_bp` | `1000000` | informative markers further apart restart the decoder |
| `bin_bp` | `1000000` | map bin width |
| `read_free_tract_sites` | `1000` | runs of at least this many zero-depth sites of a sample are uncovered for it (its calls there are imputed; 1000 sites = ten 100-SNP painting bins; chance runs are <= 15 sites in the 5x simulations, <= 604 in real tromau3 data; 0 disables) |
| `shared_family_evidence` | `True` | *Set by* `[recombination] shared_family_evidence`. fit shared sample-orientation corrections before decoding (user setting) |
| `order_breakpoints` | `()` | *Set by* `[recombination] order_breakpoints`. (contig, start, end, reason) rows of the reference-order breakpoint table (user setting). |
| **shared_orientation** (SharedOrientationConfig) |  | Screened coordinate ascent of shared sample-orientation corrections (rates per physical bp). |
| `shared_orientation.error_rate` | `1e-08` | asymmetric orientation-error CTMC prior of a sample's track orientation (entry rate per bp, mean tract length) |
| `shared_orientation.error_mean_bp` | `50000.0` | asymmetric orientation-error CTMC prior of a sample's track orientation (entry rate per bp, mean tract length) |
| `shared_orientation.maximum_candidate_bp` | `1000000` | longest candidate tract |
| `shared_orientation.minimum_incident_edges` | `2` | meioses a sample must share for its tracts to be candidates |
| `shared_orientation.maximum_sweeps` | `4` | coordinate-ascent sweeps |
| `shared_orientation.minimum_objective_gain` | `2.0` | nats a flip must gain |
| `shared_orientation.candidate_support` | `0.9` | screening posterior that marks a supported run. |
| **junctions** (JunctionConfig) |  | Bin-honest call intervals and the reference-order junction detector (bp, probabilities, nats). |
| `junctions.snapped_bin_minimum_bp` | `0` | report the two bins around a straddled painting-bin edge when they span at least this many bp (0 widens every straddled call) |
| `junctions.minimum_parents` | `3` | parents with calls at a locus |
| `junctions.hotspot_switch_probability` | `0.05` | point-hotspot part of the recombination ceiling (no single locus gives a real crossover in more than 5% of meioses beyond the background rate) |
| `junctions.flag_log_likelihood_ratio` | `4.605170185988092` | flag at 100:1 (about 30 candidate loci per genome; a ratio reaches c under its null with probability about 1/c). |

## Environment

No setting is read from the environment: every setting is in the configuration. The package reads these facts about its environment:

| variable | use |
| --- | --- |
| `NUMBA_CACHE_DIR` | Base directory for compiled kernels; the package uses a subdirectory per code version (package source, Python/NumPy/Numba/llvmlite versions, code-generation settings, CPU model). Default: a node-local scratch directory per scheduler job (or run) and host. |
| `XDG_CACHE_HOME` | Persistent kernel store `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/haplotype-reconstruction/numba` (default `~/.cache/haplotype-reconstruction/numba`); the six most recently used code versions are kept. |
| `SLURM_JOB_ID` | Scheduler job identity: scopes the automatic kernel cache directory; recorded in batch-queue claims. |
| `SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID` | Array task identity (automatic kernel cache directory). |
| `SLURM_TMPDIR` | Scratch directory of the automatic kernel cache inside a Slurm job. |
| `SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE` | The job's memory: one of the bounds of the available memory the memory governor starts from. |
| `SLURM_JOB_END_TIME` | Batch queue: the allocation end of a coordinator or helper (expired owners stop offering work; expired claims can be taken over). |
| `PBS_JOBID` | PBS job identity (automatic kernel cache directory); also `PBS_ARRAY_INDEX`, `PBS_ARRAYID`. |
| `LSB_JOBID` | LSF job identity (automatic kernel cache directory); also `LSB_JOBINDEX`. |
| `SGE_ROOT` | Marks a Grid Engine site, whose `JOB_ID` and `SGE_TASK_ID` then scope the automatic kernel cache directory. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_TIE_CENSUS` | Diagnostic, unset in normal use: a directory into which every tie decision appends its compared values (`DIR/census.<pid>.jsonl`, one JSON line per decision) for the valley census that places the tie quanta (maths/ties.py). Results do not depend on it. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_TIE_REVERSE` | Diagnostic, unset in normal use: `1` reverses every remaining arbitrary tie convention (index, content-key, default-state, sample-name and keep-first orders; maths/ties.py `reverse_conventions`), never the stated priors. The release acceptance test compares such a run with a default run: released outputs must agree outside released ambiguity. Records written under it carry `tie_reverse` in their identities and are never resumed by a default run. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_TIE_REVERSE_KEEP` | Diagnostic, with `HAPLOTYPES_TIE_REVERSE`: comma-separated names of discovery conventions (or `all`) kept at their default while the others are reversed, to attribute a reversal difference (discovery/conventions.py). The central reversals of maths/ties.py are not covered. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_COMPOUND_SCHEDULE` | Family-phase compound-update schedule: `coloured` (default) or `serial` (reference). The selected schedule is part of the family-phase checkpoint identity. This diagnostic comparison does not change priors or tolerances. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_CAVITY_MODE` | Family-phase cavity implementation: `counts` (default) or `fold` (reference). Included in checkpoint identity. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_FAMILY_WORK_BOUND` | Experimental diagnostic family-witness bound; `0` (default) keeps complete families. Positive bounds are not part of the accepted 2.3 model; bound64 was rejected. Included in checkpoint identity. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_COMPOUND_WORK_BOUND` | Experimental diagnostic compound-update bound; `0` (default) keeps the complete search. Positive bounds are not part of the accepted 2.3 model. Included in checkpoint identity. |
| `HAPLOTYPES_DISCOVERY_CLIQUE_STATS` | Diagnostic, unset in normal use: a directory into which discovery's tie-carrying residual clustering appends its alternative-pool statistics (one file per process). Results do not depend on it. |

and sets these for itself and its worker processes:

| variable | value |
| --- | --- |
| `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`, `VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS`, `NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS` | Set to 1 at package import: numerical libraries never start their own thread pools; all parallelism is explicit (Numba teams and process pools). |
| `NUMBA_THREADING_LAYER`, `OMP_WAIT_POLICY` | Set to `omp` and `PASSIVE` at package import. |
| `NUMBA_DISABLE_INTEL_SVML` | Set to 1 at package import (release 2.1): Numba's math functions use scalar libm, never Intel SVML's vector kernels, so results do not depend on the machine. |
| `NUMBA_NUM_THREADS` | Set to the run's cores at run start, so worker processes size their Numba pools from it. |
| `NUMBA_CACHE_DIR` | Set to the code-version cache directory at package import (inherited by workers). |
